q: You want every AI tool you use to already know your role and style. What does the lesson suggest?
options: Explain your role at the start of every conversation
Create a separate spec for each tool
Rely on each tool's default settings
Write one four-section spec and paste it into any tool you use
explanation: The written spec — role, style, routines and know-how — turns any tool into an assistant briefed on your world. Put the core in custom instructions, keep the full spec as a file, and paste it into new tools the day you meet them.

q: Which section of the assistant spec does the lesson call 'the gold'?
options: Role, because it defines your job
Know-how — the facts you constantly re-explain
Style, because it sets the tone
explanation: Know-how is the facts you re-explain constantly: team names, clients, current projects, deadlines. Every fact you type once is a fact you never retype.

q: You set up a morning briefing prompt. According to the lesson, where does the real value come from?
options: From the automation running it without you
From AI writing your to-do list for you
From the habit of planning your day in one place with a second pair of eyes
From having a summary of yesterday's news
explanation: The value isn't the automation; it's the habit of planning the day in one place with a second pair of eyes. The prompt surfaces what you've missed, your three priorities and what you should say no to.
